chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Nadr ibn Qirwash, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who performed tamattu' with the 'umrah up to the hajj, so the sacrificial rite became obligatory upon him. He sought it but could not find it, while he was well-off and in good condition, yet he was too weak to fast. So what should he do?
He عليه السلام said: He should pay the price of the nusuk to someone who will slaughter it in Makkah, if he intends to depart to his family, and it should be slaughtered in Dhu al-Hijjah.

So I said: If he gave it to someone to slaughter on his behalf, but he did not find a nusuk in Dhu al-Hijjah and found one after that? He عليه السلام said: He must not slaughter it on his behalf except in Dhu al-Hijjah, even if he delays it until the following year.

key_terms.الصِّيَامِ: fasting as an alternative obligation in some cases
key_terms.النُّسُكُ: the sacrificial offering required in this hajj context
key_terms.الْعُمْرَةِ: the minor pilgrimage performed before hajj in tamattu'
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: performed tamattu', combining 'umrah with hajj in the prescribed manner
key_terms.ثَمَنَ: the price or monetary value paid for the offering
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: the month in which the sacrificial act must take place

ai.seo_question: What should a well-off tamattu' pilgrim do if he cannot find the required sacrificial animal and is unable to fast?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the person performing tamattu' hajj who owes a sacrificial offering but cannot obtain it, despite being financially able and also being unable to fast. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام instructs that he should send the price to someone who will slaughter on his behalf in Makkah during Dhu al-Hijjah, and if that is not possible in that month, the slaughter is deferred to Dhu al-Hijjah of the following year.
